## Overview

The `sequence_information` specification describes an on-disk representation of a _sequence information_. 
This contains a set of reference sequences and describes the name, length, circularity, and genome of origin of each reference sequence.
It is based on the `Seqinfo` class from the [**Seqinfo** Bioconductor package](https://bioconductor.org/packages/Seqinfo).

## Object metadata

The `OBJECT` file should contain a `sequence_information` property, itself a JSON object with the following properties:

- `version`, a string specifying the version of the `sequence_information` format.
```{r, results="asis", echo=FALSE}
cat("  This should be set to \"", as.character(.version), "\".", sep="")
```

## Directory structure

### Contents 

The directory should contain: 

- `OBJECT`, a JSON file as described above.
- `info.h5`, a HDF5 file.

### `info.h5`

The `info.h5` file should contain a `sequence_information` group.

The `sequence_information` group should contain:

- `name`, a 1-dimensional string dataset. 
  This contains the names of the reference sequences.
  All entries should be unique.
- `length`, a 1-dimensional dataset of any datatype that is representable by a 64-bit unsigned integer.
  Each entry contains the length of each reference sequence in base pairs.
- `circular`, a 1-dimensional dataset of any datatype that is representable by a 32-bit signed integer.
  A non-zero value indicates that the corresponding reference sequence is circular.
- `genome`, a 1-dimensional string dataset. 
  Each entry specifies the genome of origin for each reference sequence.

The `sequence_information/name`, `sequence_information/length`, `sequence_information/circular` and `sequence_information/genome` datasets should be of the same length.
The length of each dataset represents the number of reference sequences in the _sequence information_.
The $i$-th entry from each dataset describes the $i$-th reference sequence.

Optionally, the `sequence_information/length` dataset may have a `missing-value-placeholder` attribute.
The attribute should be scalar and should have the same datatype as its dataset.
All entries in the dataset equal to the placeholder value should be treated as missing.

Optionally, the `sequence_information/circular` dataset may have a `missing-value-placeholder` attribute.
The attribute should be scalar and should have the same datatype as its dataset.
All entries in the dataset equal to the placeholder value should be treated as missing.

Optionally, the `sequence_information/genome` dataset may have a `missing-value-placeholder` scalar string attribute.
All entries in the dataset equal to the placeholder value should be treated as missing.
